# Just the results, please

# Context

I have been recently tinkering with `get_item_details()` function of the ParlAT package. While a few things are still in flux (it’s version 0.0.4 after all), the main development is the inclusion of the `votes` parameter into the function arguments. When set to TRUE the function now returns the voting result of the provided item ('Verhandlungsgegenstand') in its third reading in the National Council ('dritte Lesung im Nationalrat'). 

To get a clear picture of what I mean, look at this [example](https://www.parlament.gv.at/gegenstand/XX/I/1833){target="_blank"} from the website of the Austrian Parliament. 

![Voting result in the National Council in the third reading on Gefahrgutbeförderungsgesetz, Änderung (1833 d.B.)](_data/ScreenshotVotingResultWebsite.png)

The `get_item_details()`  parses the data which lie behind the graph on the voting results. 

Note that not every item type is actually subject to votes; not every item on which can be voted in fact reaches the third reading; and votes prior to the third reading are (at least for now) not returned.  If the item does not feature a vote or a third reading, the returned vote column returns NULL. I emphasize this so that the scope of what the function can deliver and what not is clear.

To demonstrate the parameter’s utility, I will query in this blog post the parties’ votes since the 20th legislative period (1996) until now, and will check:

1. How often do parties vote in favor or against an item in the third reading (relative frequency per legislative period)?
2. With which other party does a party vote (either in favor or against)?
3. What is the relative frequency of party-combinations for in-favor and not-in-favor votes for the different legislative periods?

As you will see, the querying of the relevant data is rather straightforward. Most of the code presented was needed to create the three graphs, so don’t get distracted by this. 

And before I finally dive into the actual code, the usual caveat apply a) this is work in progress, if you see any error, have suggestion etc. do not hesitate to contact me with feedback ([repo forum](https://github.com/werkstattcodes/ParlAT/discussions){target="_blank"} or [bluesky direct msg](https://bsky.app/profile/zoowalk.bsky.social){target="_blank"}); b) although  I am developing the ParlAT package, I don’t consider myself as an expert on the ins-and-outs of the Austrian Parliament. The main motivation is to provide a tool which makes researching the Austrian Parliament a bit easier, c) this is a blog post and does not pretend to be an academic output etc.

To give you an overview of the code, essentially, there are three steps needed (more details below):

1. use `get_items()` to get a dataframe of the items for the legislative periods in question
2. feed the urls of the obtained items as input to the `get_item_details(vote = TRUE)` query
3. wrangle and filter the data and produce the graphs. 

Enough rambling. Let's dive in...


# Packages

Get the necessary packages. 

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Load packages and configure parallel plan"
library(ParlAT)
library(tidyverse)
library(reactablefmtr) #table formater
library(reactable) #creation of reactables
library(ggupset) #upsetter plots
library(ggtext) #text formatting in ggplots
library(tidytext)
library(furrr) #apply functions in parallel
library(patchwork) #combine multiple plots into one
```

# Get items
## Query data

To start with, let's get all items for the legislative periods 20 to 28. No big deal.

```{r}
#| label: fetch-items
#| code-summary: "Fetch National Council items and cache them"
#| cache: true
#| eval: false
items_20_28 <- seq(20, 28) %>%
  map(., \(x) get_items(legis_period = x, institution = "NR")) %>%
  list_rbind()
nrow(items_20_28)
```
 
```{r}
#| include: false
# readr::write_rds(
#   items_20_28,
#   here::here(
#     "posts",
#     "2026-05-21-ParlAT-votingPatterns",
#     "_data",
#     "items_20_28.rds"
#   )
# )
items_20_28 <- readr::read_rds(here::here(
  "posts",
  "2026-05-21-ParlAT-votingPatterns",
  "_data",
  "items_20_28.rds"
))
```

To get an overview of the (relative) frequency of the different item types, 
let's transform this data into two tables.

## Fequency Tables

```{r}
#| label: summarise-items
#| include: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Read cached item data and inspect item types"
# Use the available legislative periods as dynamic table columns and set a compact table theme.
period_cols <- sort(unique(items_20_28$legis_period))
compact_table_theme <- reactablefmtr::fivethirtyeight(font_size = 12)
table_source <- reactablefmtr::html(
  "<span style=\x27font-size:8pt;color:grey30;font-family:Segoe UI !important;line-height:0.5\x27>Source: www.parlament.gv.at. Analysis: Roland Schmidt - @zoowalk - https://werk.statt.codes</span>"
)

style_reactable_table <- function(table, title, subtitle = NULL) {
  styled_table <- table %>%
    reactablefmtr::add_title(
      title = reactablefmtr::html(paste0(
        "<span style=\x27font-size:12pt;\x27>",
        title,
        "</span>"
      ))
    )

  if (!is.null(subtitle)) {
    styled_table <- styled_table %>%
      reactablefmtr::add_subtitle(
        subtitle = reactablefmtr::html(paste0(
          "<span style=\x27font-size:10pt;line-height:0.5;\x27>",
          subtitle,
          "</span>"
        )),
        font_color = "grey30",
        font_weight = "normal",
        font_style = "italic"
      )
  }

  styled_table %>%
    reactablefmtr::add_source(source = table_source)
}

# Format legislative-period columns as right-aligned integer counts for the first table.
period_count_cols <- setNames(
  map(
    period_cols,
    \(period) {
      colDef(
        align = "right",
        format = colFormat(separators = TRUE, digits = 0),
        na = ""
      )
    }
  ),
  period_cols
)

# Format legislative-period columns as right-aligned percentage shares for the second table.
period_share_cols <- setNames(
  map(
    period_cols,
    \(period) {
      colDef(
        align = "right",
        format = colFormat(digits = 1, suffix = "%"),
        na = ""
      )
    }
  ),
  period_cols
)

# Count document types per legislative period and reshape to one row per document type.
type_abs_counts <- items_20_28 %>%
  count(legis_period, type_doc_long, type_doc) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(type_doc_long, type_doc),
    names_from = legis_period,
    values_from = n
  )

# Calculate each document type as a percentage of all items within its legislative period.
type_rel_counts <- items_20_28 %>%
  count(legis_period, type_doc_long, type_doc) %>%
  mutate(rel = n / sum(n), .by = legis_period) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(type_doc_long, type_doc),
    names_from = legis_period,
    values_from = rel
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) x * 100))

# Render the document-type counts as a compact interactive table.
type_abs_counts_table <- reactable(
  type_abs_counts,
  columns = c(
    list(
      type_doc_long = colDef(
        name = "Document type",
        align = "left",
        minWidth = 320,
        filterable = TRUE,
        sticky = "left"
      ),
      type_doc = colDef(
        name = "Code",
        align = "left",
        minWidth = 80,
        filterable = TRUE,
        sticky = "left"
      )
    ),
    period_count_cols
  ),
  fullWidth = TRUE,
  compact = TRUE,
  highlight = FALSE,
  outlined = TRUE,
  defaultPageSize = 23,
  defaultSorted = "XXVIII",
  defaultSortOrder = "desc",
  theme = compact_table_theme
) %>%
  style_reactable_table(
    "ITEM TYPES BY LEGISLATIVE PERIOD",
    "Absolute number of each item type per legislative period. Data as of 29 May 2026."
  )

# Render the document-type percentage shares as a compact interactive table.
type_rel_counts_table <- reactable(
  type_rel_counts,
  columns = c(
    list(
      type_doc_long = colDef(
        name = "Document type",
        align = "left",
        minWidth = 320,
        filterable = TRUE,
        sticky = "left"
      ),
      type_doc = colDef(
        name = "Code",
        align = "left",
        minWidth = 80,
        filterable = TRUE,
        sticky = "left"
      )
    ),
    period_share_cols
  ),
  fullWidth = TRUE,
  compact = TRUE,
  highlight = FALSE,
  outlined = TRUE,
  defaultPageSize = 23,
  defaultSorted = "XXVIII",
  defaultSortOrder = "desc",
  theme = compact_table_theme
) %>%
  style_reactable_table(
    "ITEM TYPES BY LEGISLATIVE PERIOD",
    "Share of each type within all items in the legislative period. Data as of 29 May 2026."
  )
```

## Keep items of interest

The get_item() call from above returned all (!) items. When interested in votes in the third reading, only a subset of items is relevant. Below we filter for them. In case I missed any category here, please let me know.

```{r}
#| label: define-item-scope
#| code-summary: "Select legislative item types for voting analysis"
items_select <- c("^A$", "RV", "BUA", "GABR", "GABR13", "BRA", "^EBR$") %>%
  paste0(., collapse = "|")

items_scope <- items_20_28 %>%
  filter(str_detect(type_doc, regex(items_select)))

items_scope %>%
  distinct(type_doc_long, type_doc)
```


```{r}
#| label: item-scope-freq-table
#| code-summary: "Frequency table on item types for voting analysis"
#| column: page-right
#| eval: false
#| include: false
# Show the selected document types as percentage shares within each legislative period.
items_scope_doc_shares <- items_scope %>%
  count(legis_period, type_doc_long, type_doc) %>%
  mutate(rel = n / sum(n), .by = legis_period) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(type_doc, type_doc_long),
    names_from = legis_period,
    values_from = rel
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) x * 100))

# Render the scoped document-type shares with the same compact table style as above.
items_scope_doc_shares_table <- reactable(
  items_scope_doc_shares,
  columns = c(
    list(
      type_doc = colDef(
        name = "Code",
        align = "left",
        minWidth = 80,
        filterable = TRUE,
        sticky = "left"
      ),
      type_doc_long = colDef(
        name = "Document type",
        align = "left",
        minWidth = 320,
        filterable = TRUE,
        sticky = "left"
      )
    ),
    period_share_cols
  ),
  fullWidth = TRUE,
  compact = TRUE,
  highlight = FALSE,
  outlined = TRUE,
  defaultPageSize = 23,
  defaultSorted = "XXVIII",
  defaultSortOrder = "desc",
  theme = compact_table_theme
) %>%
  style_reactable_table(
    "SELECTED DOCUMENT TYPES FOR VOTING ANALYSIS",
    "Share of the selected vote-relevant document types within each legislative period. Data as of 29 May 2026."
  )

items_scope_doc_shares_table
```

# Get item details

## Single case example

Before using our above obtained results to query to voting results, it might be instructive to demonstrate the return value of the new vote paramete with a single example. The item is the one for which we saw above the results. Note that the return value is a list column.

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Single case vote results"
#| code-fold: false
example <- get_item_details(
  item_url = "https://www.parlament.gv.at/gegenstand/XX/I/1833?selectedStage=105",
  votes = TRUE
)

#content of votes list column
example$votes

#content of interest
example$votes[[1]]$result %>% select(text, infavor)
```

So as you can see from above, the returned votes column is a list column which contains
again the list column `result`. From here, we can extract the party name (`text`) and the vote result (`infavor`). (Note, in a later version the function might get further streamlined so that the return value is already the nested result).

## Query data

To continue with our dataset from the 20th legislative period onwards, let's extract the urls of the items and feed them to `get_item_details()` with votes set to TRUE. I wrap the function call in purrr's `safely` to collect any
potential errors; and use `future_map()` to query the API with multiple workers simultaneously, i.e. to speed up the process. 

```{r}
#| label: fetch-item-details
#| code-summary: "Fetch item details with voting results and cache them"
#| cache: true
#| eval: false
plan(multisession, workers = 4)

item_urls <- items_scope %>%
  pull(item_url)

safe_get_item_details <- safely(get_item_details)

item_details_raw <- item_urls %>%
  future_map(
    \(x) {
      safe_result <- safe_get_item_details(item_url = x, votes = TRUE)
      safe_result$item_url <- x
      safe_result
    },
    .progress = TRUE,
    .options = furrr_options(packages = c("ParlAT", "purrr", "tibble"))
  )
```
 
```{r}
#| eval: true
#| include: false
# readr::write_rds(
#   item_details_raw,
#   here::here(
#     "posts",
#     "2026-05-21-ParlAT-votingPatterns",
#     "_data",
#     "item_details_raw.rds"
#   )
# )

# plan(sequential)

item_details_raw <- readr::read_rds(here::here(
  "posts",
  "2026-05-21-ParlAT-votingPatterns",
  "_data",
  "item_details_raw.rds"
))
```

Below, I a) check for any failed calls, and b) combine the successful calls into a single dataframe.

```{r}
#| label: prepare-vote-agreement-data
#| code-summary: "Build party agreement matrix from cached vote details"
#check failed function calls
failed_items <- item_details_raw %>%
  keep(\(x) !is.null(x$error)) %>%
  map(\(x) {
    tibble(
      item_url = x$item_url,
      error = conditionMessage(x$error)
    )
  }) %>%
  list_rbind()
nrow(failed_items)

#combine successful calls into one single dataframe
items_details <- item_details_raw %>%
  keep(\(x) is.null(x$error)) %>%
  map("result") %>%
  list_rbind()
```

As we can see, there were `r nrow(failed_items)` failed item calls.
As already discussed, `get_item_details()` returns the vote results as a nested list column. Hence, it's content has to be unpacked. 

As an intermediate step, let me cross-tabulate the presence of item votes and the procedural stage of the item. Remember that not every item does necessarily (yet) feature a vote during the third reading.

```{r}
#| code-summary: "How many items have a vote"
#add vote presence indicator
items_details <- items_details %>%
  mutate(votes_present = map_lgl(votes, \(x) !is.null(x)))

vote_yn <- items_details %>%
  count(votes_present) %>%
  mutate(rel = n / sum(n))
vote_yn


items_details %>%
  #filter(votes_present) %>%
  select(status_number, status_description, votes_present, item_url) %>%
  count(status_number, votes_present)

table(items_details$status_number, check$votes_present)
```

As it turns out, `r scales::percent(vote_yn %>% filter(votes_present) %>% pull(rel), accuracy = 1)` of all items feature a vote. If we cross-tabulate this with status number (which is part of the API response), we see that almost all items with a vote are of category 5, i.e., are concluded. 

So what about the other items which are also of status 5, but do not feature a vote. Unfortunately, at least that's my current understanding, there is no explicit return value indicating whether an item has reached the third reading. However, `get_item_details` also includes that 'stages' parameter which returns one row for each stage. The column `stage_name` has a description of the stage, and this can be searched for the presence of 'dritte Lesung'/third reading.

Here the stages for our single case example:

```{r}
#|code-summary: "Example: check for third reading"
example$stages[[1]]

example$stages[[1]] %>%
  filter(str_detect(stage_name, regex("dritte Lesung", ignore_case = T))) %>%
  pull(stage_name)
```

Let's use this approach to check for our full `items_details` dataset. For this, I'll use an auxiliary function

```{r}
items_details <- items_details %>%
  mutate(third_reading=map_lgl(stages, \(x) x %>% str_detect(stage_name, regex("dritte Lesung", ignore_case=T))))
  
```






```{r}
items_votes <- items_details %>%
  unnest_wider(votes, names_sep = "_")
class(items_votes$votes_result)

items_votes <- items_votes %>%
  filter(map_lgl(votes_result, \(x) !is.null(x))) %>%
  unnest(votes_result)

items_votes <- items_votes %>%
  select(
    item_url,
    type = type_doc,
    title,
    item_number,
    item_url,
    legis_period,
    text,
    code,
    party_infavor = infavor
  )
```

# Graphic 1: Relative Frequency of vote type

```{r}
items_votes <- items_votes %>%
  mutate(
    text = case_when(
      legis_period == "XXV" & text %in% c("NEOS", "NEOS-LIF") ~ "NEOS/NEOS-LIF",
      legis_period == "XXVI" & text %in% c("JETZT", "PILZ") ~ "JETZT/PILZ",
      TRUE ~ text
    ),
    code = case_when(
      legis_period == "XXV" & text == "NEOS/NEOS-LIF" ~ "NEOS/NEOS-LIF",
      legis_period == "XXVI" & text == "JETZT/PILZ" ~ "JETZT/PILZ",
      TRUE ~ code
    ),
    vote_id = paste(legis_period, item_url, sep = "|")
  )

items_voted_n <- items_votes %>%
  distinct(legis_period, vote_id) %>%
  count(legis_period, name = "items_voted_n")

votes_contested <- items_votes %>%
  group_by(vote_id, legis_period, item_url) %>%
  summarise(vote_types_n = length(unique(party_infavor))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(contested = if_else(vote_types_n > 1, "contested", "not contested"))

table(votes_contested$legis_period, votes_contested$contested)

# self-join to get party-pary combinations
items_votes_combi <- items_votes %>%
  left_join(., items_votes, by = "vote_id", suffix = c("_x", "_y")) %>%
  mutate(
    agreement = if_else(
      party_infavor_x == party_infavor_y,
      "agreement",
      "disagreement"
    )
  )

agreement_matrix <- items_votes_combi %>%
  #  filter(text_x != text_y) %>%
  group_by(legis_period_x, text_x, text_y, agreement, .drop = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(
    agreement_n = n(),
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    agreement_share = agreement_n / sum(agreement_n),
    .by = c(legis_period_x, text_x, text_y)
  ) %>%
  filter(agreement == "agreement")

agreement_matrix_wide <- agreement_matrix %>%
  select(legis_period_x, text_x, text_y, agreement_share) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = text_y, values_from = agreement_share)

gov_parties <- tribble(
  ~legis_period , ~text   , ~gov_rank ,
  "XX"          , "SPÖ"   ,         1 ,
  "XX"          , "ÖVP"   ,         2 ,
  "XXI"         , "ÖVP"   ,         1 ,
  "XXI"         , "F"     ,         2 ,
  "XXII"        , "ÖVP"   ,         1 ,
  "XXII"        , "F"     ,         2 ,
  "XXII"        , "F-BZÖ" ,         3 ,
  "XXIII"       , "SPÖ"   ,         1 ,
  "XXIII"       , "ÖVP"   ,         2 ,
  "XXIV"        , "SPÖ"   ,         1 ,
  "XXIV"        , "ÖVP"   ,         2 ,
  "XXV"         , "SPÖ"   ,         1 ,
  "XXV"         , "ÖVP"   ,         2 ,
  "XXVI"        , "ÖVP"   ,         1 ,
  "XXVI"        , "FPÖ"   ,         2 ,
  "XXVII"       , "ÖVP"   ,         1 ,
  "XXVII"       , "GRÜNE" ,         2 ,
  "XXVIII"      , "ÖVP"   ,         1 ,
  "XXVIII"      , "SPÖ"   ,         2 ,
  "XXVIII"      , "NEOS"  ,         3
)

party_order <- agreement_matrix %>%
  distinct(legis_period = legis_period_x, text = text_x) %>%
  left_join(gov_parties, by = c("legis_period", "text")) %>%
  mutate(is_gov = !is.na(gov_rank)) %>%
  group_by(legis_period) %>%
  arrange(!is_gov, gov_rank, text, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(party_order = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

agreement_matrix_ordered <- agreement_matrix %>%
  left_join(
    party_order %>%
      transmute(
        legis_period_x = legis_period,
        text_x = text,
        is_gov_x = is_gov,
        party_order_x = party_order
      ),
    by = c("legis_period_x", "text_x")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    party_order %>%
      transmute(
        legis_period_x = legis_period,
        text_y = text,
        is_gov_y = is_gov,
        party_order_y = party_order
      ),
    by = c("legis_period_x", "text_y")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    text_x = reorder_within(text_x, party_order_x, legis_period_x),
    text_y = reorder_within(text_y, party_order_y, legis_period_x)
  )

items_label_str <- items_scope %>%
  distinct(type_doc, type_doc_long) %>%
  arrange(type_doc) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(type_doc_long, " (", type_doc, ")")) %>%
  pull(label) %>%
  paste(collapse = ", ")

legis_period_fn <- getExportedValue(
  "ParlAT",
  if ("get_legis_period" %in% getNamespaceExports("ParlAT")) {
    "get_legis_period"
  } else {
    "get_legis_periods"
  }
)

legis_period_labels <- legis_period_fn() %>%
  filter(
    legis_period_abbrev %in% unique(agreement_matrix_ordered$legis_period_x)
  ) %>%
  left_join(items_voted_n, by = c("legis_period_abbrev" = "legis_period")) %>%
  mutate(
    years = if_else(
      is.na(date_end),
      paste0(format(date_start, "%Y"), "-present"),
      paste0(format(date_start, "%Y"), "-", format(date_end, "%Y"))
    ),
    label = paste0(
      "<span style=\"font-size:13pt; font-weight:700;\">",
      legis_period_abbrev,
      "</span><br>",
      "<span style=\"font-size:10pt; font-weight:400;\">",
      years,
      "</span><br>",
      "<span style=\"font-size:9pt; font-weight:400;\">Number of items voted on: ",
      scales::number(items_voted_n, accuracy = 1),
      "</span>"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(name = legis_period_abbrev, value = label) %>%
  tibble::deframe()

data_cutoff <- {
  d <- max(items_20_28$date, na.rm = TRUE)
  paste0(
    scales::ordinal(as.integer(format(d, "%d"))),
    " of ",
    format(d, "%B %Y")
  )
}

label_vec_x <- agreement_matrix_ordered %>%
  distinct(text_x, is_gov_x) %>%
  mutate(
    party = str_remove(as.character(text_x), "___.*$"),
    label = if_else(is_gov_x, paste0("<b>", party, "</b>"), party)
  ) %>%
  select(name = text_x, value = label) %>%
  mutate(name = as.character(name)) %>%
  tibble::deframe()

label_vec_y <- agreement_matrix_ordered %>%
  distinct(text_y, is_gov_y) %>%
  mutate(
    party = str_remove(as.character(text_y), "___.*$"),
    label = if_else(is_gov_y, paste0("<b>", party, "</b>"), party)
  ) %>%
  select(name = text_y, value = label) %>%
  mutate(name = as.character(name)) %>%
  tibble::deframe()
```
 


 
```{r}
#| label: plot-party-vote-shares
#| code-summary: "Stacked party vote-position shares"
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 10
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"
#| dev: svglite
max_party_slots <- max(party_order$party_order, na.rm = TRUE)
legis_period_levels <- sort(unique(party_order$legis_period))

party_vote_shares <- items_votes %>%
  distinct(vote_id, legis_period, text, party_infavor) %>%
  count(legis_period, text, party_infavor, name = "votes_n") %>%
  mutate(vote_share = votes_n / sum(votes_n), .by = c(legis_period, text)) %>%
  left_join(party_order, by = c("legis_period", "text")) %>%
  mutate(
    party_slot = party_order,
    vote_stance = if_else(party_infavor, "In favour", "Not in favour"),
    vote_stance = factor(vote_stance, levels = c("In favour", "Not in favour")),
    vote_share_label = if_else(
      vote_stance == "Not in favour" & vote_share >= 0.04,
      scales::percent(vote_share, accuracy = 1),
      NA_character_
    ),
    legis_period = factor(legis_period, levels = sort(unique(legis_period)))
  )

party_vote_axis_labels <- party_order %>%
  mutate(
    party = str_remove(text, "___.*$"),
    party = str_replace_all(party, "/", "/<br>"),
    label = if_else(is_gov, paste0("<b>", party, "</b>"), party),
    legis_period = factor(legis_period, levels = legis_period_levels)
  )

p_party_vote_shares <- party_vote_shares %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = party_slot, y = vote_share, fill = vote_stance)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_text(
    data = party_vote_shares %>% filter(vote_stance == "Not in favour"),
    aes(y = vote_share / 2, label = vote_share_label),
    colour = "white",
    size = 3,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  ggtext::geom_richtext(
    data = party_vote_axis_labels,
    aes(x = party_order, y = -0.07, label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3.1,
    label.colour = NA,
    fill = NA,
    label.padding = grid::unit(rep(0, 4), "pt"),
    lineheight = 0.95,
    vjust = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~legis_period,
    ncol = 3,
    labeller = labeller(legis_period = as_labeller(legis_period_labels))
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq_len(max_party_slots),
    limits = c(0.5, max_party_slots + 0.5),
    labels = NULL,
    expand = expansion(mult = 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("In favour" = "#1b9e77", "Not in favour" = "#d95f02"),
    breaks = c("Not in favour", "In favour"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1), clip = "off") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Share of votes",
    title = "Party vote positions",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Share of selected Nationalrat third-reading item votes cast in favour or not in favour, ",
      "by parliamentary party group and legislative period. Government parties are bold and ordered first."
    ),
    caption = paste0(
      "Voting on the following items was included: ",
      items_label_str,
      "<br><br>Data: www&#46;parlament.gv.at via ParlAT package, as of ",
      data_cutoff,
      "<br>Graphic: Roland Schmidt, https&#58;//werk.statt.codes <span style=\"color:#1185FE;\">&#x1F98B; @zoowalk</span>"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.caption.position = "panel",
    plot.title = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      size = 18,
      face = "bold",
      margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 8)
    ),
    plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(
      size = 13,
      lineheight = 1.15,
      margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 4, b = 14)
    ),
    plot.caption = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(
      hjust = 0,
      halign = 0,
      size = 10,
      lineheight = 1.1,
      margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 8)
    ),
    strip.text = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 13, hjust = 0),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.justification = "left",
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 8, r = 8, b = 34, l = 8)
  )

p_party_vote_shares
```

# Graph 3: Upset Plot

```{r}
#| label: plot-upset-period-percent
#| code-summary: "Percentage UpSet plots by legislative period and vote type"
#| column: page
#| fig-width: 18
#| fig-height: 28
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"
vote_sets_percent <- items_votes %>%
  distinct(vote_id, legis_period, text, party_infavor) %>%
  summarise(
    parties = list(sort(unique(text))),
    .by = c(vote_id, legis_period, party_infavor)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    vote_stance = if_else(party_infavor, "In favour", "Not in favour"),
    vote_stance = factor(vote_stance, levels = c("In favour", "Not in favour"))
  ) %>%
  count(legis_period, vote_stance, parties, name = "votes_n") %>%
  mutate(
    vote_share = votes_n / sum(votes_n),
    .by = c(legis_period, vote_stance)
  )

vote_stance_levels <- levels(vote_sets_percent$vote_stance)

make_period_upset_plot <- function(period, vote_type) {
  period_parties <- party_order %>%
    filter(legis_period == period) %>%
    arrange(party_order) %>%
    pull(text)

  show_column_title <- period == first(legis_period_levels)
  show_row_title <- vote_type == first(vote_stance_levels)

  label_data <- vote_sets_percent %>%
    filter(legis_period == period, vote_stance == vote_type) %>%
    mutate(
      vote_share_label = if_else(
        vote_share >= 0.05,
        scales::percent(vote_share, accuracy = 1),
        NA_character_
      )
    )

  panel_data <- label_data %>%
    mutate(vote_share_piece = vote_share / votes_n) %>%
    tidyr::uncount(votes_n)

  panel_data %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = parties, y = vote_share_piece, fill = vote_stance)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.75) +
    geom_text(
      data = label_data,
      aes(y = vote_share / 2, label = vote_share_label),
      colour = "white",
      size = 4.4,
      fontface = "plain",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +
    scale_x_upset(
      sets = period_parties,
      n_intersections = Inf,
      order_by = "freq"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("In favour" = "#4575b4", "Not in favour" = "#d73027"),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
      limits = c(0, NA),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
    ) +
    labs(
      title = if_else(show_column_title, as.character(vote_type), ""),
      x = NULL,
      y = if_else(show_row_title, period, "")
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme_combmatrix(
      combmatrix.label.text = element_text(size = 7),
      combmatrix.panel.point.size = 1.8
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        size = 11,
        hjust = 0.5,
        face = "bold",
        margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 4)
      ),
      axis.title.y = element_text(
        angle = 0,
        hjust = 1,
        vjust = 0.5,
        face = "bold",
        size = 10,
        margin = ggplot2::margin(r = 8)
      ),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 4, r = 4, b = 4, l = 4)
    )
}

period_vote_type_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  legis_period = legis_period_levels,
  vote_stance = vote_stance_levels
)

period_upset_plots <- map2(
  period_vote_type_grid$legis_period,
  period_vote_type_grid$vote_stance,
  make_period_upset_plot
)

p_upset_period_percent <- wrap_plots(
  period_upset_plots,
  ncol = length(vote_stance_levels)
) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Which party combinations voted together?",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Rows show legislative periods; columns show whether the party combination voted in favour or not in favour. ",
      "Bars show each party combination share within that row-column vote universe."
    ),
    caption = paste0(
      "Voting on the following items was included: ",
      items_label_str,
      "<br><br>Data: www&#46;parlament.gv.at via ParlAT package, as of ",
      data_cutoff,
      "<br>Graphic: Roland Schmidt, https&#58;//werk.statt.codes @zoowalk"
    ),
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        hjust = 0,
        size = 18,
        face = "bold",
        margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 8)
      ),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        hjust = 0,
        size = 13,
        margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 12)
      ),
      plot.caption = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(
        hjust = 0,
        halign = 0,
        size = 10,
        lineheight = 1.1,
        margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 8)
      )
    )
  )

p_upset_period_percent
```



## Results

The agreement matrix reveals a consistent and striking pattern across all nine legislative periods: **coalition membership is by far the strongest predictor of voting alignment**, consistently producing agreement rates of 97–100% between governing parties, regardless of their ideological distance.

### Grand coalition dominance (XX, XXIII, XXIV, XXV)

In the four periods where SPÖ and ÖVP governed together, their agreement rates were near-perfect: 99.3%, 98.7%, 100%, and 98.9% respectively. This consistency is remarkable — across more than two decades and very different political contexts, the two parties voted in lockstep whenever they shared government. XXIII (2007–2008) is worth a brief note: a short transitional grand coalition after the collapse of the Schüssel II government, its SPÖ–ÖVP rate of 98.7% falls squarely in line with the others. What is notable in XXIII is that BZÖ and FPÖ — the two right-wing parties that had split in 2005 — still showed 77.5% alignment with each other in opposition, suggesting their ideological divergence had not yet fully materialised in voting behaviour.

### The FPÖ government experiment (XXI, XXII)

The ÖVP–FPÖ coalition under Schüssel produced equally tight coalition discipline: 99% in XXI and a perfect 100% in XXII. In XXII the FPÖ split into FPÖ and BZÖ mid-term — yet both splinter groups maintained 100% alignment with ÖVP, confirming both stayed in government. In opposition, SPÖ and GRÜNE found each other with \~83–85% alignment.

### A counterintuitive finding in XX

In the XX period (1996–1999), FPÖ under Haider was in opposition — and voted more closely with GRÜNE (70%) and the Liberal Forum (69%) than with either SPÖ (36%) or ÖVP (36%). For a right-wing populist party, this level of alignment with the Greens is striking, and likely reflects that opposition parties of any stripe frequently voted against the grand coalition's proposals regardless of ideology.

### The first Türkis-Blau coalition (XXVI)

The 2017–2019 ÖVP–FPÖ coalition under Sebastian Kurz produced an FPÖ–ÖVP agreement rate of 96.4% — high, but notably below the 100% seen in XXII. More striking is what happened to SPÖ: after voting in lockstep with ÖVP throughout the grand coalition years (98.9% in XXV), their agreement rate collapsed to just 42% in XXVI — the sharpest single-period drop in the entire dataset. The new opposition also saw the emergence of PILZ (later JETZT), which aligned closely with SPÖ at 90%, forming a de facto left bloc against the governing coalition.

### The Türkis-Grün experiment (XXVII)

The ÖVP–Greens coalition of 2019–2024 is perhaps the most remarkable case in the dataset. Despite being natural ideological opponents on many issues, ÖVP and GRÜNE achieved 100% voting agreement in parliament — identical to the most disciplined grand coalitions. Meanwhile FPÖ in opposition showed only 56% alignment with ÖVP, its lowest in any period where the two were not governing together. The opposition bloc (FPÖ, SPÖ, NEOS) was relatively undifferentiated, all clustering around 56–68% agreement with each other.

### The current Dreierkoalition (XXVIII)

The three-party ÖVP–SPÖ–NEOS coalition formed in 2024 shows near-perfect internal cohesion: ÖVP–SPÖ at 100%, ÖVP–NEOS at 98.6%, SPÖ–NEOS at 98.6%. FPÖ, now the sole opposition party, is clearly isolated — agreeing with governing parties only 37–38% of the time, the lowest opposition score across the entire dataset. GRÜNE, also in opposition, sit at \~69% with the coalition, positioning themselves as a more moderate opposition voice.

::: callout-note
The high overall agreement rates are partly a function of item type selection. Bills that reach a floor vote — especially treaty ratifications and budget items — tend to pass with broad consensus. Contested votes would show more differentiation.
:::
